tasks.title: Lecture #20
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an environmental science class.
tasks.transcript:
Professor: Biomimicry is the human practice of learning from and imitating things found in nature in order to create new inventions. This way, scientists and engineers can create innovative solutions that are both efficient and sustainable.
One well- known example of biomimicry is the development of a widely used fastening system. The inventor was inspired by the way burrs, uh thorns, from plants stuck to his dog’s fur. By replicating the tiny hooks found on the burrs he removed from the dog fur, he created the new fastening system. Another example is the design of energy- efficient buildings based on the ventilation system of structures created by termites. Termites are ground- dwelling insects that use different materials to create hills, or mounds, in which the termites live. Termite mounds have a complex network of vents. The vents maintain a stable internal temperature, which can be emulated in human architecture.
Biomimicry can also be applied to renewable energy. For instance, researchers are developing wind turbine blades modeled after the flippers of humpback whales. The unique shape of the flippers reduces drag and increases efficiency, leading to more effective wind energy capture.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: Ways in which humans use natural materials in clothing and architecture
options.C: New methods of using renewable energy
options.D: Examples of how humans imitate nature for practical purposes

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：这段讲话主要讲了什么？ 定位原文： Biomimicry is the human practice of learning from and imitating things found in nature in order to create new inventions. ... One well-known example of biomimicry is the development of a widely used fastening system. ... Another example is the design of energy-efficient buildings based on the ventilation system of structures created by termites. ... Biomimicry can also be applied to renewable energy. For instance, researchers are developing wind turbine blades modeled after the flippers of humpback whales. 选项分析： A. Ways in which humans use natural materials in clothing and architecture（人类在服装和建筑中使用天然材料的方式）。讲话讨论的是模仿自然界的结构和机制，而非使用天然材料，所以A选项错误。 B. Hiding strategies of different animals（不同动物的隐藏策略）。基于讲话未涉及动物隐藏策略，所以B选项错误。 C. New methods of using renewable energy（使用可再生能源的新方法）。可再生能源只是讲话中提到的一个应用领域，并非主要内容，所以C选项错误。 D. Examples of how humans imitate nature for practical purposes（人类为了实用目的模仿自然的例子）。讲话围绕仿生学的定义展开，并列举了魔术贴、白蚁窝通风系统、鲸鱼鳍片等多个例子，因此D选项正确。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention a dog?

options.A: To illustrate how an inventor copied animal behavior
options.B: To compare its efficiency in movement with that of humpback whales
options.C: To explain how a structure found in plants inspired an invention
options.D: To show the close bond between scientists and animals

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：演讲者为什么提到狗？ 定位原文： The inventor was inspired by the way burrs, uh thorns, from plants stuck to his dog’s fur. By replicating the tiny hooks found on the burrs he removed from the dog fur, he created the new fastening system. 选项分析： A. To illustrate how an inventor copied animal behavior（为了说明发明家如何模仿动物行为）。讲话中模仿的对象是植物（牛蒡）的结构，而非狗的行为，所以A选项错误。 B. To compare its efficiency in movement with that of humpback whales（为了将其运动效率与座头鲸进行比较）。基于讲话未提及狗的运动效率，也未与鲸鱼比较，所以B选项错误。 C. To explain how a structure found in plants inspired an invention（为了解释植物中的一种结构如何启发了一项发明）。讲话指出发明家受到牛蒡刺粘在狗毛上的启发，通过复制牛蒡上的微小钩子创造了魔术贴，因此C选项正确。 D. To show the close bond between scientists and animals（为了展示科学家与动物之间的紧密联系）。讲话未讨论科学家与动物的关系，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about termite mounds?

options.A: The temperature inside of them does not change much.
options.B: Termites sometimes build them near human-made structures.
options.C: Building them takes a lot of energy.
options.D: They are created mostly from plant material.

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：演讲者对白蚁丘提出了什么观点？ 定位原文： Termite mounds have a complex network of vents. The vents maintain a stable internal temperature, which can be emulated in human architecture. 选项分析： A. The temperature inside of them does not change much（它们内部的温度变化不大）。讲话指出白蚁丘的通风网络能够维持稳定的内部温度，因此A选项正确。 B. Termites sometimes build them near human-made structures（白蚁有时会在人造结构附近建造白蚁丘）。基于讲话未提及白蚁丘的位置，所以B选项错误。 C. Building them takes a lot of energy（建造它们需要大量能量）。讲话未讨论建造所需的能量，所以C选项错误。 D. They are created mostly from plant material（它们主要由植物材料建造）。讲话提到白蚁使用不同的材料建造土丘，但未说明主要成分，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker imply about wind turbine blades that are being developed?

options.A: The noise they create can be harmful to whales.
options.B: They can be easily installed on buildings.
options.C: They can be efficiently constructed from renewable materials.
options.D: They are very similar to some whales’ flippers in shape.

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：演讲者对正在研发的风力涡轮机叶片有什么暗示？ 定位原文： For instance, researchers are developing wind turbine blades modeled after the flippers of humpback whales. The unique shape of the flippers reduces drag and increases efficiency, leading to more effective wind energy capture. 选项分析： A. The noise they create can be harmful to whales（它们产生的噪音可能对鲸鱼有害）。基于讲话未提及噪音问题，所以A选项错误。 B. They can be easily installed on buildings（它们可以很容易地安装在建筑物上）。讲话未讨论安装位置，所以B选项错误。 C. They can be efficiently constructed from renewable materials（它们可以用可再生材料高效建造）。讲话未提及建造材料，所以C选项错误。 D. They are very similar to some whales' flippers in shape（它们的形状与某些鲸鱼的鳍状肢非常相似）。讲话明确指出叶片是以座头鲸的鳍状肢为模型设计的，因此D选项正确。
